subject: Web Technologies & Internet / PHP
question: What is the difference between the Internet and the World Wide Web?
option_a: The Internet is the global network infrastructure; the Web is a service (HTTP pages) running on it
option_c: The Web is the hardware cables
explanation: The Internet is the physical/logical network connecting computers; the WWW is one application over it (HTTP/HTML), along with email, FTP, DNS etc.

question: Which HTTP method should be used to submit data that creates a new resource on the server?
explanation: POST sends data in the body for processing/creation. GET retrieves; PUT replaces a resource at a URL (idempotent); HEAD returns headers only.

question: What does CSS specificity mean?
option_a: Rules with higher specificity override lower-specificity rules for the same element
explanation: Specificity ranks selectors (id > class/attribute/pseudo-class > type). Higher specificity wins on conflict; ties go to the later rule.

subject: Web Technologies & Internet / PHP
question: Compared with a cookie, a server-side session has which property?
option_a: Session data stays on the server; the client holds only a session identifier (usually a cookie)
option_b: Session data is stored entirely in the browser
option_d: Sessions are slower to read on the server always
explanation: Sessions keep state server-side keyed by an ID the client sends (in a cookie or URL). Cookies can hold data client-side and are size/security limited.

option_d: POST must always return HTML pages
explanation: REST uses HTTP verbs on resources: GET read, POST create, PUT/PATCH update, DELETE remove. Responses are usually JSON.

subject: Web Technologies & Internet / PHP
question: Which statement correctly distinguishes server-side from client-side processing?
option_a: Server-side code runs on the web server (e.g. PHP, Node); client-side code runs in the browser (e.g. JavaScript)
option_b: PHP always runs in the browser
option_c: JavaScript always runs on the server
option_d: HTML is processed by the server only
explanation: Server-side executes on the server before the response is sent; client-side executes in the user's browser after the page loads.

subject: Web Technologies & Internet / PHP
question: What is an SQL injection attack?
option_a: Injecting malicious SQL via user input that is concatenated into queries without sanitization
explanation: SQLi occurs when untrusted input is embedded in SQL. Prepared statements/parameterized queries prevent it. XSS and DoS are different attacks.

subject: Web Technologies & Internet / PHP
question: Which defence is most effective against stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)?
option_a: Output-encoding/escaping user content and validating input before rendering
option_c: Disabling JavaScript only in the admin panel
explanation: XSS injects scripts via unescaped output. Encode untrusted data on output (context-aware) and validate on input; use CSP as defense in depth.
